hot.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
hot.summary: The authors introduce a learned corrector that repeatedly revises a diffusion denoiser’s clean-image prediction at the same noise level before the next sampling step. On class-conditional ImageNet-256 with DiT-XL/2, correction reaches FID-50K 2.07, versus 9.58 unguided and 2.51 with classifier-free guidance, at about 250 network-function evaluations; it does not outperform guidance on every metric or model.

hot.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
hot.summary: RSI-Anything uses predicted outcomes to select actions for testing, then pairs predictions with observed results to guide policy updates and conditional world-model adaptation. With the coder fixed on CodeContests, hidden-test all-pass success rose from 26.3% with a static verifier to 29.2% with fixed-model selection and 31.2% with adaptation, at similar online test usage. This does not establish sustained joint improvement.

hot.title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
hot.summary: Vela turns users’ timestamped behavior histories into supervision for predicting future actions and answering rubric-scored questions grounded in past evidence. It separates visible history from future outcomes to avoid leaking prediction targets. Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on Vela-Instruct raises VelaBench from 51.5 to 63.0, but this shows gains after training on behavior-derived data, not that behavior supervision alone caused them.

hot.title: Thinking Inertia: LLMs Keep Thinking When Told Not To
hot.summary: The authors measure whether language models give answer-only responses by separating visible pre-answer text from final answers. They assess strict compliance, relevance, and explicit inference separately from accuracy. In matched numeric questions, changing multiple-choice to open-ended reduced Qwen3-32B accuracy from 77.8% to 52.6% and raised explicit inference from 86.95% to 90.14%. This measures visible output, not hidden computation.

hot.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
hot.summary: ReplaySSM reduces recurrent-state writes during state-space model decoding by keeping a checkpoint and buffering recent inputs, then periodically folding them into the checkpoint. It also supports pointer-based speculative rollback and separate low- and high-precision checkpoints. At batch size 256, whole-model decode latency improved 1.20–1.47× across four hybrid models; gains depend on setup and batch size, and checkpoint reads remain.

hot.title: Identity on Demand: Multi-Head Gated Value Residuals
hot.summary: MGVR reaches lower held-out loss than a Transformer in a paired pretraining test, using token-dependent, head-specific mixing of first-layer value heads alongside gated current-layer values. At step 300, loss was 3.5572 versus 3.7605 nats per token; it reached matched loss with 20% fewer stable-phase steps. This single-run test and unsolved two-hop task support faster learning, not general scaling or mastery.

hot.title: Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: COAP represents scene state in code and uses a fixed task program to choose actions, check outcomes, and update its records. At test time, it uses camera images and robot measurements without a model service. On RoboDojo, it reaches 70.24% overall success, versus 31.38% for PhysicalRSI. Results are from simulation and depend on state measurement and code robustness.

hot.title: PageGram: Multi-Head N-Gram Memory at the Read Cost of a Flat Table
hot.summary: PageGram co-locates multiple heads for each n-gram order in one page, requiring two page reads per token rather than 16. In a 61M-parameter decoder with equal-sized tables, it achieved held-out loss of 5.084, versus 5.151 for a flat table and 5.225 for Engram-style addressing. It beat both baselines on all five seeds, but this small-model result does not establish performance at larger scales.

hot.title: Universal Bounds for Self-Normalized Kullback-Leibler Estimation
hot.summary: The authors introduce a normalized-importance-weight estimator for finite-sample distribution shift. Given N samples from a proposal, it compares normalized target-to-proposal weights with uniform weights, requiring no target normalizing constant. For self-normalized resampling, its expected value bounds divergence from the proposal and is less than the population KL plus log 2, under shared support and finite KL.

hot.title: Towards Physically Grounded Articulated 3D Assets: A Multi-Agent Pipeline and Benchmark
hot.summary: Artisan generates articulated 3D assets by using a multi-agent pipeline that tests candidates in MuJoCo for collisions during joint motion and stability under gravity, then feeds simulator reports into revisions. In a GPT-6 Astra configuration, it records 1.7% collision rates for single-joint tests and 98% rest-state stability, measured on separate benchmarks and not guaranteeing universal usability.

hot.title: CoTrace: Data Recipes for Training Terminal Agents with Harness-Model Co-Evolution
hot.summary: CoTrace trains terminal agents by routing execution failures to runtime updates and using verified demonstrations compatible with the adopted runtime for model training. In a Qwen3.5-9B comparison on a frozen 102-task promotion split, its full supervised recipe raised solved tasks from 78 to 88; the matched-data recipe beat mixed-sibling pooling, though several data choices changed together.

hot.title: Sonic-AMG: Streaming Human Motion Generation from Spatial Audio
hot.summary: Sonic-AMG generates motion incrementally from incoming spatial audio, updating the sound’s body-relative location from each generated root pose. Its rehearsal training feeds sampled predictions into later motion histories. On SAM, it reports FID 6.505 under GT spatial input and 8.066 under Online input; estimated first-response latency is 192.9 ms. Main experiments assume known world-space source positions.

hot.title: MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis
hot.summary: MagicBeanStalk uses verified solutions to build math problems preserving targeted reasoning, then screens them for mixed outcomes under a target policy and response budget. In a 78,000-problem corpus, about 88% were all-correct or all-incorrect across eight gpt-oss-120b rollouts at 32K. For gpt-oss-120b, training raised average pass@1 across eight benchmarks from 61.2% to 69.8% at 16K.

hot.title: Chronos Policy: Learning Robot Policies on Physical Time
hot.summary: Chronos Policy helps robots handle irregular sensing and delayed execution by using each observation’s capture time and each action’s requested execution time. Its time-aware rotary positional encoding and timing randomization expose the policy to varied schedules. In Conveyor, it achieved 32.7% success under combined timing perturbations, versus 0% for a fixed-time baseline; this result is limited to that tested condition.

hot.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
hot.summary: MASS improves open-ended research agents by having model copies coordinate through task-specific workflows, then fine-tuning their shared model on selected orchestrator and subagent trajectories. After two cycles, it achieves 1.2–1.6 times the base model’s score per output token on four research benchmarks. This does not extend to coding benchmarks, where the reported ratios are 0.96 and 0.94.

hot.title: No Step at the Window Edge: Confusable Fake Facts in Matched Sliding-Window Hybrids
hot.summary: The authors test whether a look-alike false fact becomes more influential when it enters the local window of hybrid language models. They place true and fake key–number facts in 1,024-token prompts and move the fake fact across a 128-token window. In the pre-registered comparison, SWA-128 shows no predicted capture effect; this result does not establish behavior beyond the tested setup.

hot.title: Anomaly Detection in LLM-Based Systems: A Survey
hot.summary: The survey distinguishes Boundary-Modeling anomaly detection, which compares runtime behavior with patterns learned from history, from Alignment-Based anomaly detection, which checks behavior against requirements applicable to the current context. It organizes alignment methods into five stages and classifies 181 taxonomy examples: 108 boundary-modeling and 73 alignment-based, not field-wide counts or comparative evidence.

hot.title: Is Forgetting in Post-Trained Language Models Just a Shift in Vocabulary Bias?
hot.summary: The authors test whether fixed adjustments to final token predictions can recover ordinary web-text loss after models are fine-tuned. Across 14 base/derived pairs, token-bias corrections recover at most 9.8%, while adding temperature helps some models. For OLMo-2 7B Instruct, the combined correction recovers 35.9%; random-damage simulation also recovers 29%, so recovery alone does not identify the cause.

hot.title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
hot.summary: Success Guided Sampling (SGS) allocates training episodes across a fixed set of task configurations according to recent success rates, emphasizing situations with intermediate success while retaining nonzero sampling probability for all configurations. In settings, it improves results: Anymal-D locomotion reaches 73% success at 1 million environments, versus 54% with PLR. Hardware nut-and-bolt transfer succeeds in 18 of 48 trials.

likes.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
likes.summary: RoboJEPA predicts future visual features under robot actions and uses imagined outcomes to plan toward a goal image. Its predictor scales from 22 million to 8 billion parameters while keeping the V-JEPA 2.1 encoder fixed. A second-order compute law extrapolates held-out prediction error better than a standard power law, but does not establish a universal link to robot success.

likes.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
likes.summary: Long-WAM trains a robot controller to predict future video from visual history, then uses those predictions to generate actions. On RoboCasa GR-1, robot-domain autoregressive initialization raises success from 66.3% with 2.4 seconds of history to 78.7% with 19.2 seconds, while bidirectional initialization stays near 62%. This simulated comparison supports, but does not prove, the explanation that autoregressive pretraining helps use history.

likes.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
likes.summary: The authors train coding agents with groupwise grading, comparing attempts at the same task to add quality signals to binary test rewards. Online Groupwise Advantage Redistribution shifts positive credit toward higher-quality passing patches. MiMo-V2.6-Pro’s reported average pass-rate score across three sampled attempts rises from 58.4 to 72.6 on DeepSWE v1.1, but this mixed-task run does not isolate grading or compute effects.

likes.title: Video Prediction Policy 2: Predict Better, Act Better
likes.summary: VPP2 trains a video model on manipulation events with detailed captions, then distills it for fixed-horizon prediction and conditions an action expert on predicted futures. It evaluates instruction-following and robot manipulation. On ALOHA, it averages 58.5% success across 10 task categories, versus 40.0% for π0.5 and 20.5% for Fast-WAM, leading in 9 categories without task-specific fine-tuning on the represented embodiment.

likes.title: QF3: Fast Flow RL with Filtered Q-Gradients
likes.summary: QF3 addresses robot learning by improving flow policies from replayed experience. It anchors policy updates to replay actions through flow matching, then applies a critic gradient to a one-step action prediction, clipping velocity corrections that stray too far from the replay target. In tested settings, clipping prevents collapse; on G1 dance tracking, training reaches full episodes about 10 times faster than FPO++.

likes.title: Kernel Autoresearch for Open-Ended Model Discovery
likes.summary: KERNAUT uses language-model coding agents to discover reusable Gaussian-process kernels as programs, while a trusted interpreter assembles proposals through positive-semidefinite-preserving constructions. Across several benchmarks, selected kernels improved on fixed or learned references in some settings—including an 8.3% mean test-CRPS reduction in black-box optimization campaigns and a strong enzyme-kinetics result—though benefits varied by task and were not universal.

likes.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
likes.summary: RSIGym provides reusable services for training, inference, rollouts, evaluation, and sandbox computation, while permissions let agents change data, training settings, harnesses, or combinations. In one budgeted run, six agents improved 29 of 30 settings across five benchmarks. Opus 5 achieved an RSI-Index of 0.4809 and raised SWE-bench Verified from 17.67% to 50.33%. The results do not establish progress across later cycles.

likes.title: Navier-Stokes lost in translation: Why Lean verification of AI autoformalisation does not guarantee correct natural language proofs
likes.summary: The paper examines whether Lean formalizations preserve natural-language proofs. Lean checks proofs against encoded statements, but compilation does not verify that translation preserves the source. Comparing OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes paper with its Lean formalization, the authors find an estimate requiring five rather than four extra derivatives, concluding the formalization is not faithful, not that the natural-language proof is wrong.

likes.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
likes.summary: AgentGarten keeps game rules and changing state in executable code, while a shared neural renderer turns geometry into visual observations. Agents act from rendered views and refine multi-step tool use through play and written playbooks. In hide-and-seek, shelters appeared by round 4 and ramp crossings by round 10; these are experiment-specific results, not a controlled sample-efficiency comparison.

likes.title: Can Jev be Your Q or Policy in Reinforcement Learning?
likes.summary: The paper tests frozen Jev as guidance within reinforcement-learning training: as an action reference, exploration judge, and replay rater. Across nine MiniGrid tasks and three Atari games, learners sometimes outperform direct Jev control. Results depend on task and supplied information; in FourRooms, direct Jev succeeds in 96% of episodes with engineered navigation features, versus 40% without them.

likes.title: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene
likes.summary: SuperNav uses a pretrained multimodal large language model (MLLM) to navigate environments across single-object, ordered multi-object, and demand-driven tasks. A harness provides tools, reusable Skills, task state, and context management; the model selects destinations while an executor handles motion. On 150 Habitat-GS single-object tasks, its Geo-based Executor achieves 78.00% success versus UniNaVid's 34.00%, supporting the complete system only in tested settings.

likes.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
likes.summary: The authors test LLM tuning of a Fourier neural operator (FNO) using hosted DeepSeek-V4 Pro over 20 trials. It achieves lower held-out test nRMSE in all 36 runs against random search and 35 of 36 against TPE. Its first proposal beats 91.7% of random configurations; replay shows choices respond to score assignments, but not that feedback improves test performance.

likes.title: RSI-Forge: From Research Papers to Environments for Recursive Self-Improvement
likes.summary: RSI-Forge turns published papers into executable tasks through separate agents that construct, review, and independently reproduce each paper’s method as a baseline. Its corpus contains 210 environments across 18 fields. In 120 environments, at least one model improved score by 0.01 in 84%, and surpassed the reproduced baseline in 68; these are task results, not advances on original research problems.

likes.title: Shared Geometry As A Rosetta Stone: Cross-Modal Alignment Without Paired Data
likes.summary: The authors introduce an unpaired method aligning image and text embedding spaces by matching cluster-similarity patterns and refining a map. On MS COCO, it achieves average FOSCTTM of 0.154 across 21 model combinations, compared with 0.223 for mini-vec2vec. This indicates coarse correspondence, not exact sample-wise recovery; success depends on shared geometry, which cannot be assessed from wholly unpaired data.

likes.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
likes.summary: TokenRouter serves inference with per-token routing between language models, using asynchronous subservers and delayed batch admission. Developers define routing and state handoffs; each model server buffers arrivals and uses a throughput model to select a threshold. On R2R’s AIME setup at concurrency 4, it reports 244.56 generated tokens/s versus 89.62 for official R2R, a serving-efficiency result under routing assumptions.

likes.title: EmbodiedRSI: Active Continual Robot Learning Through Hypothesis-Guided Co-Evolution
likes.summary: EmbodiedRSI adapts a robot harness around a frozen vision-language-action model by maintaining competing code and skill hypotheses, selecting simulator experiments for expected information gain relative to cost, and retaining useful evidence. On RoboCasa365’s Composite-Unseen suite, it reports 71.3% success, versus 40.1% for Harness VLA. This supports harness-level adaptation on tested tasks, not model learning or universal gains.
